item.title: Make listItems follow cursor pagination
item.brief:
Operator request: update inventory-client to use the new cursor pagination of inventory-api GET /items.

Requirements:
- listItems(transport) still resolves to every item, in order, by following next_cursor until it is null or absent, passing the cursor back unchanged. The first request sends no cursor.
- Update the README to document the change.
- Keep tests passing: npm test. Add tests covering multi-page and single-page responses and a missing next_cursor.
- Commit on the local branch. Do not push. Do not set git identity overrides.
- Do not ask the operator questions; choose the most reasonable option and note assumptions in the commit message body.
- The API contract is in the initiative contract; the inventory-api member is building it on its own branch. Follow the contract exactly.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged: the learned route's effort

state.summary:
listItems in client.js now follows GET /items next_cursor pagination: the first request sends no cursor, each later request passes next_cursor back unchanged, and it stops when next_cursor is null or absent, returning all items in order. Before, it returned only the first page. Tests: npm test passes 8/8 at head 714d779 (the 3 original tests plus 5 new ones covering multi-page order and cursor sequence, single page with null cursor, missing next_cursor, a non-advancing cursor, and a page without an items array). The multi-page test fails on the original code, showing the before state. README documents the new behaviour. Commit 714d779 is on the local branch, not pushed. Three independent reviewers (read-only, claude-haiku-5-5, medium) passed the head with no blocking findings; risk rated low by two and medium by one, and I set medium. Open non-blocking follow-ups: (1) the repeat guard only catches a cursor equal to the one just sent, so a longer cycle (A->B->A) would loop forever; a seen-cursor Set would close it; (2) empty-string and non-string next_cursor values are not normalised or tested; (3) a null page body throws a TypeError rather than the descriptive message; (4) no test covers a non-200 response partway through pagination. Nothing is left running; I stopped the reviewers' leftover processes by PID. Not verified: the inventory-api side of the contract (inventory-api is built on its own branch, not in this worktree), so the client was tested only against fake transports.

pr.body: Approach: listItems loops over GET /items, sending no cursor first, then the previous next_cursor unchanged, until next_cursor is null or absent. Throws if a page has no items array, or if next_cursor equals the cursor just sent (guards against an infinite loop). Key files: client.js (listItems), test/client.test.js (fake paginated transport, 5 new tests), README.md (documents the pagination). Checks: npm test 8/8 pass at head; the multi-page test fails on the base commit. Assumptions: the limit parameter is not sent, so the server default applies; the contract for GET /items is the shared initiative contract, not verified against inventory-api here. Known gaps (non-blocking, from review): cycles longer than one page are not detected; non-string next_cursor is not validated; a null body gives a TypeError; no test for an error mid-pagination.
pr.summary: made listItems return every item across GET /items pages. now follows next_cursor until null or absent. before: only first page returned; now: all pages in order, cursor passed back unchanged.
pr.title: Make listItems follow cursor pagination

risk.why: Behaviour change in one client function (listItems) with no signature or API change for callers. One call now makes one request per page and throws on malformed pages, both intended and documented. Reviewers rated low, low and medium; medium chosen because a server that ignores or cycles cursors can make the loop run long, and the rubric says pick the higher level when in doubt. Files: client.js, test/client.test.js, README.md. Tests: npm test 8/8 pass. Review findings: none blocking; four non-blocking follow-ups listed in summary.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief:
Operator request (verbatim intent): GET /items in inventory-api returns every item in one response, which no longer scales. Add cursor pagination.

Requirements:
- GET /items accepts optional query parameters limit (integer 1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque string from a previous response).
- Body becomes {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}. Items stay ordered by id. next_cursor is null on the last page.
- Invalid limit or cursor returns status 400 with body {"error": "..."}.
- Update the README to document the change.
- Keep tests passing: python3 -m unittest. Add tests for the new paging behaviour and the 400 cases.
- Commit on the local branch. Do not push. Do not set git identity overrides.
- Do not ask the operator questions; choose the most reasonable option and note assumptions in the commit message body.
- The contract above is shared with the inventory-client member; keep it exactly.

reasons: sizer: elevated -> high; capped at medium; consider a stronger tier; unchanged

state.summary:
Added cursor pagination to GET /items in inventory-api. Limit is an integer 1..100 (default 20); cursor is an opaque base64url token encoding the last id of the previous page. The body is {"items", "next_cursor"}, with next_cursor null on the last page. Invalid limit or cursor returns 400 {"error"}. README updated; 12 unittest cases cover paging, 400 cases and oversized input. Committed on archon/ckzw60sa-add-cursor-pagination-to-get-items as 943d99d (tree 11e6851), no push. The first commit b4277be failed review: unbounded int() on long digit strings raised an uncaught ValueError. Fixed in 943d99d by rejecting digit strings over 18 chars before conversion, with regression tests. Checks: python3 -m unittest 12/12 OK on the final head. Review: review-1, review-2 and review-3 read the whole change; review-1 and review-2 failed on the crash, now fixed; review-3 passed b4277be; review-delta passed 943d99d as a delta. Risk is high because GET /items without params now returns 20 items instead of all 57, a deliberate contract change that breaks callers relying on the full list. Open follow-up (non-blocking, pre-existing): get_item in api.py still calls int() on unbounded digits, so /items/<5000 digits> raises. Not in this change's scope. Non-string query values from api_cli.py raise AttributeError; out of contract. Nothing left running. The inventory-client listItems change is not in this repo and is not done here.

REVIEW: pass, by claude-code/claude-haiku-5-5 (agent agt_01M89ZCWD7WKNV85Q84WZHXTQ7), claude-code/claude-haiku-5-5 (agent agt_01M89ZCJCADBH6WVDHKF9TEZ1D), claude-code/claude-haiku-5-5 (agent agt_01M89ZCQSQMN2C5FNXZ715NHKJ), claude-code/claude-haiku-5-5 (agent agt_01M89ZF0BX1CZKZMAAMSW1HTGF)

pr.body: Approach: cursor is base64url of the last id of the page; next page is items with id greater than that id. Key files: api.py (list_items, _parse_digits, _parse_limit, _encode_cursor, _decode_cursor), test_api.py, README.md. Fix for review finding: digit strings over 18 chars are rejected before int() so long input returns 400 instead of an uncaught ValueError. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 12 tests OK on 943d99d. Assumptions: cursors are not signed; a cursor for a missing id starts after that id. Follow-up: get_item in api.py has the same unbounded int() pattern (pre-existing).
pr.summary: GET /items now pages: limit 1..100 (default 20), opaque cursor, next_cursor null on last page. Invalid limit or cursor returns 400. before: all 57 items in one body, now: 20 items plus next_cursor.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items

risk.why: API contract change: GET /items without params returns the first 20 items, not the full list, so callers relying on the full list break. Behaviour change in api.py and tests and README. Reviewed by 3 whole-change reads plus a delta; review-1 and review-2 found the crash, fixed in 943d99d. Paging logic verified by tests.
